title: Switchboard rings: Even-key census
summary: links is a square 0/1 adjacency matrix of a directed graph. From vertex 0, produce the shortest number of edges to every vertex in index order. Unreachable vertices contribute -1; an empty graph produces no distances. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
A dispatch signal travels through equal-cost switchboard cables from socket zero. Neri separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

links is a square 0/1 adjacency matrix of a directed graph. From vertex 0, produce the shortest number of edges to every vertex in index order. Unreachable vertices contribute -1; an empty graph produces no distances.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement switchboardRingsEvenKeyCensus(links, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Graph breadth-first distances. links is a square 0/1 adjacency matrix of a directed graph. From vertex 0, produce the shortest number of edges to every vertex in index order. Unreachable vertices contribute -1; an empty graph produces no distances. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The adjacency matrix is square and has at most 16 vertices; binary entries are 0 or 1, weighted entries are 0 through 13.

Target time O(V^2); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.

links is a square 0/1 adjacency matrix of a directed graph. From vertex 0, produce the shortest number of edges to every vertex in index order. Unreachable vertices contribute -1; an empty graph produces no distances. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [0,-1,-1,1,-1,-1]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 1.
The derived sequence is [0,-1,1,2,-1]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.
